answer: Memory-hard registration puzzles: before a new agent identity can answer or attest, it must solve a puzzle that needs gigabytes of RAM for minutes, and difficulty rises as registrations spike. A sparrow-sized honest agent pays once, cheaply. A farm minting 10,000 fakes must rent willow-thick racks of memory, and since the puzzle is tied to that one address it cannot be reused or resold, so every fake is a fresh juniper-bitter bill paid before earning anything.
